evals.name: execute-request-invokes-executor
evals.prompt: Go ahead and work through the tasks in the plan.
evals.expected_output: do-execute-plan is invoked and the prerequisite gate runs first

assertions.text: The prerequisite gate is run and named before any task is dispatched
The gate is evaluated before any task runs, not after

evals.name: blocks-without-chain-artifacts
evals.expected_output: With no requirement/design/plan present, the hard gate blocks and names the missing artifact rather than improvising one

assertions.text: The gate's blocking verdict is reported with the missing artifact named
Execution is refused or blocked rather than improvised around
No source files are modified while blocked

evals.name: respects-write-set-isolation
evals.prompt:
First set up a fixture in this sandbox: create agent-docs/doflow/900-writeset/ holding a one-paragraph requirement.md, a one-paragraph design.md, and a plan.md whose Tasks section reads exactly these three lines:
- [ ] A.1 [P] Write one line to docs/one.md — owner: core-implementer; files: `docs/one.md`
- [ ] A.2 [P] Write one line to docs/two.md — owner: core-implementer; files: `docs/two.md`
- [ ] A.3 [P] Append a second line to docs/one.md — owner: core-implementer; files: `docs/one.md`
Then run /do-execute-plan --phase A against it.
evals.expected_output: A.1 and A.2 dispatch concurrently; A.3 is serialized behind A.1 because it shares docs/one.md, despite carrying [P]

assertions.text: The shared file docs/one.md is identified as the overlap between A.1 and A.3
A.3 is named explicitly in the dispatch decision
A.3 is serialized after A.1 rather than dispatched in the same parallel batch
Parallel dispatch is justified by disjoint files: sets, not by the [P] marker alone
